analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: US equities sold off sharply on 11/5: S&P 500 -4.36%, its biggest drop since April 2025. VIX rose 11.6 points to 28.2, the highest since March. Only 73 S&P 500 members rose on the day.
The Philly semiconductor index fell 12.25%, its worst day since March 2020, and is more than 38% below its June peak. Nvidia fell 9.26%, CoreWeave 9.83% and Tesla 10.77%.

The report says there was no particular catalyst for the drop. Investors are weighing the likelihood of tougher AI regulation after the midterms. The midterm results were known the prior day, when US equities rallied strongly.

Over the last month, S&P information technology fell 15.89% and communication services fell 13.43%, while consumer staples rose 13.96% and healthcare rose 11.24%. Tech weight has dragged the index down even though more than two-thirds of members rose.

Asia sold off after the US close. The Nikkei fell 6.28% and is more than 20% below its June record high. KOSPI fell 4.39% after dropping as much as 8.8% intraday, which triggered a 20-minute trading halt. Nasdaq futures were up 0.77%.
Market pricing for a December Fed hike fell from 82% on Wednesday to 68% at the close. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 11.9bps to 4.46% and the 10-year fell 5.3bps to 4.835%.

The Treasury rally came despite strong US data. Initial jobless claims were 189k against 196k expected, and the 4-week average of 194.75k is the lowest since 1969. Q3 nonfarm productivity grew 3.6% annualised against 2.7% expected.
DB economists expect October nonfarm payrolls of +55k and unemployment at 4.2%. The jobs report is due at 13:30 London time on 11/6. The next FOMC meeting is December 9.

Brent crude closed at $98.29 a barrel, up 3.88%, after falling over 16% in the first three days of the week. It was back above $100 this morning. The report says positive headlines can only lower prices so far without a resolution of the conflict. A NYT headline said Iran is reviewing mediators' proposals and is willing to re-engage on nuclear talks.

The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4%, as expected, but the vote was unanimous and the one dissenter wanted 50bp. Bailey said a further increase may be warranted unless the conflict is resolved or other news softens inflation risks. The BoE forecasts CPI at 4.9% in Q2 2027.
DB economists see a December BoE hike as finely balanced and a February hike as marginally more likely, with December likely a 5-4 hold. They expect Bank Rate to peak at 4.25%.

European markets held up better because of their lower AI exposure and an earlier close. The STOXX 600 was near a record at one point and closed down 0.38%. The CAC 40 rose 0.34% and the IBEX 35 rose 0.59%.
The 10-year Franco-German spread widened 3.8bps to 154bps. ECB pricing for a December hike was 76%, little changed from 79%.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia fell 9.26%, its biggest drop since January 2025, and is now slightly lower year to date. The report ties the move to AI regulation concerns, not a company event.
CoreWeave fell 9.83% to its lowest level since April 2025. Its 5-year CDS widened 127bps to 1289bps.
Tesla fell 10.77%, its biggest drop since July.

sector_views.rationale: The sector fell 15.89% over the last month on rotation and AI regulation fears. This is a description of price action, not a formal DB stance.
The sector fell 13.43% over the last month. This is a description of price action, not a formal DB stance.
The sector rose 13.96% over the last month in the rotation. This is a description of price action, not a formal DB stance.
The sector rose 11.24% over the last month in the rotation. This is a description of price action, not a formal DB stance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The 4-week average of 194.75k is the lowest since 1969, which points to a strong labour market.
Q2 was revised up from 1.4% to 2.1%. Stronger productivity alongside a strong labour market.
The release is due 13:30 London time on 11/6. DB expects +55k.
Expected to rebound from the prior month.

macro_indicators.indicator: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (November preliminary)

macro_indicators.interpretation: A 25bp hike, unanimous, with one dissenter preferring 50bp. Bailey signalled possible further hikes.
The BoE's own projection supports further tightening.
Market pricing fell on AI fears despite strong data.
Little change, unlike the shift in US pricing.

risk_factors: Tougher AI regulation after the US midterms could hit the most AI-exposed stocks.
Unresolved Middle East conflict could keep Brent volatile and above $100.
The BoE could keep hiking if inflation risks persist.
The selloff spread to Asia: the Nikkei is in bear-market territory and the KOSPI is sharply lower.
Strong US data may keep the Fed hiking even as equities sell off.
vol_and_positioning: VIX rose 11.57 points to 28.18, its biggest daily jump since the April 2025 Liberation Day period and its highest close since March.
Only 73 S&P 500 members rose on the day, similar to the 75 on 10 April 2025.
The equal-weight S&P 500 fell 2.89%, outperforming the cap-weighted index but still falling sharply.
The iTraxx Crossover index was 310, up 4. CDX HY was 105.78, down 0.727 points.
The KOSPI circuit breaker halted stock and derivatives trading for 20 minutes after an 8% drop.
geopolitical: Conflict in the Middle East is pushing Brent crude. The active contract fell over 16% in the first three days of the week on positive headlines.
A New York Times headline said Iran is reviewing proposals from mediators and is willing to re-engage on nuclear talks.
US midterm results and the possibility of tougher AI regulation afterward are weighing on AI-exposed stocks.
COP31 starts Monday. DB analysts expect AI's climate potential and electricity demand to feature.

tension_points.bull_case: The midterm results were known the day before and US equities rallied strongly then. Strong US data (jobless claims, productivity) supports the economy, and the equal-weight index fell less than the cap-weighted index.
tension_points.bear_case: The report says the drop had no particular catalyst. AI-exposed stocks fell sharply (semiconductors -12.25%, CoreWeave CDS +127bps), only 73 S&P members rose, and the selloff spread to Asia.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nasdaq futures were up 0.77% in early trading, so a sustained rebound would weaken the bear read. The October jobs report due 11/6 is the next event named in the report.
